_comment: ORGANISATION risk-by-domain model for scripts/osint/exposure_score.py (--model organisation), documented in analysis/weight-engine.md §8. ANALYST-SCORED, never automatic: each domain is rated exploitability 0-3 x harm 0-3 by an analyst, the pair is mapped onto 0-10 through score_matrix, and the overall score is the mean of the RATED domains. A score is analyst judgement on a fixed scale, NOT a probability. Vocabulary and thresholds only, never case data (RULE 1).

settings._comment: rating_max bounds both axes. rationale_required_harm: a domain rated at this harm or above MUST carry <d>_rationale. min_coverage_ratio: below this share of rated domains the output carries a coverage warning. decimals: rounding of every score (half-up).

domains._comment: id -> {name, guide}. Order is the report order. Extensible: add an id here and it becomes ratable and counts towards coverage.total.

affiliates.name: Affiliate, member and partner compromise
affiliates.guide: member or affiliate organisations whose own exposure gives a path into, or harm to, the organisation

impersonation.name: Impersonation and fraud industry
impersonation.guide: lookalike domains, fake profiles and apps, brand abuse, fraud kits and campaigns using the organisation's name

edge.name: Network edge and remote access
edge.guide: internet-facing VPN, RDP, mail, admin panels, unpatched edge appliances with public exploits

insider.name: Insider and channel abuse
insider.guide: staff or contractor misuse, abuse of support / sales / partner channels, data sold from inside

personnel.name: Key personnel and leadership
personnel.guide: executives and key staff whose public exposure enables targeting, pretexting or coercion

actors.name: State actors and criminal markets
actors.guide: documented interest of state actors, ransomware crews or access brokers in the organisation or its sector

credentials.name: Staff credentials
credentials.guide: staff identifiers and passwords in breach corpora and infostealer logs, credential reuse

suppliers.name: Suppliers and partners
suppliers.guide: third-party services and vendors inferable from DNS, mail and documents, and their known compromises

mail_dns.name: Certificates, email and domains
mail_dns.guide: SPF / DMARC / DKIM posture, spoofability, dangling records, certificate and registrar hygiene

code_docs.name: Code, apps and documents
code_docs.guide: public repositories, secrets in code, mobile apps, document metadata and leaked internal files

score_matrix._comment: exploitability (row key) -> [score at harm 0, 1, 2, 3]. Default = (e x h) / 9 x 10, rounded to one decimal. Edit a cell to re-weight a combination; every row must have rating_max + 1 cells within 0..score_max.

bands._comment: Lower bound (inclusive) -> level, evaluated highest first: >= 8.0 Critical, >= 6.0 High, >= 4.0 Medium, below 4.0 Low.

priorities._comment: Remediation priority -> deadline, as printed in the report.

rubric._comment: What each rating level means, printed by --list and mirrored in analysis/weight-engine.md §8.

exploitability.0: not reachable from the internet, or no known way to use it
exploitability.1: reachable only with prior access or insider position; no public tooling; no known in-the-wild use
exploitability.2: reachable from the internet with effort; public tooling or technique exists; sporadic in-the-wild use
exploitability.3: directly reachable from the internet; commodity tooling; active in-the-wild use against similar targets

harm.0: no meaningful effect on data, operations, partners or reputation
harm.1: limited: low-sensitivity data, brief local disruption, minor reputational noise
harm.2: significant: personal or business data exposed, service disruption, partners affected, media attention
harm.3: severe: large-scale or sensitive data loss, prolonged outage, partner or member compromise, lasting reputational damage
